name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  July 20, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Pro Tem
MacLean at 5:09 p.m., on July 20, 2009 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on July 15, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  Mayor Ury (arrived at 5:11 p.m.)

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

INVOCATION: Council Member Ledesma

Mayor Ury arrived at 5:11 p.m.

CLOSED SESSION

City Council Minutes  1  July 20, 2009
 CS1. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are
  the City and City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's Negotiator is Dennis
  Wilberg.
CS2. Public Employee Performance Evaluation for the Position of City Attorney
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

  At the hour of 5:11 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem MacLean declared a recess to Closed Session.
  The City Council reconvened at 6:04 p.m., with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

  City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was no reportable action from Closed
  Session.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize Citywide Volunteers for Their 1,000 Hours of Volunteer Service

  Mayor Ury presented Certificates of Appreciation to (1) Leslie Cromwell for volunteer
  hours at the Norman P. Murray Community & Senior Center, (2) Lila Gertz for volunteer
  hours at the Norman P. Murray Community & Senior Center, (3) Trish Kuhns for
  volunteer hours at the Norman P. Murray Community & Senior Center, and (4) Nellie
  Domenick for volunteer hours at the Mission Viejo Library.

P2.  Presentation by Assemblyman Jeff Millers Office to the Dedicated Animal Welfare
  Group and Sharon Cody for Their Efforts in Raising Money to Help in the Care of
  Homeless Companion Animals at the Mission Viejo Animal Services Center

  Sharon Cody and members of DAWG received a Certificate of Recognition from Mark
  Lee, on behalf of Assemblyman Jeff Miller, for DAWG’s dedication in bettering the lives
  of animals at the Mission Viejo Animal Services Center.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

  R.J. Hansen, M.V.: referred to a recent edition of Congressman Miller’s Weekly Update
  which outlined the poor condition of California roads and complained about the condition
  of streets in Mission Viejo. He also noted that the former trash can cleaning service by
  "Clean a Can" was pricey but a better solution than washing debris down the storm

City Council Minutes  2  July 20, 2009
   drains. He recommended that the service could be included in the Waste Management
  contract.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that he has seen a proliferation of door to door
  solicitation over the past 3 to 6 months. He asked if a solicitor’s exception letter was
  legitimate and he wondered if the City Council could address a no-exception policy.

  City Attorney Curley responded that solicitors have first amendment rights. The City has
  an ordinance that regulates solicitation but cannot prohibit it. Mr. Curley recommended
  that posting a "no solicitation" sign on private property should be honored and if a
  solicitor violates that posting, there would be grounds to contact the Sheriff’s
  Department.

  Kime Goodrum, M.V.: spoke in support of the Tennis Center improvements and
  encouraged the City Council to move forward with the budget this evening.

  Wil Garcia, M.V.: asked the City Council to approve the budget, including the Tennis
  Center upgrades.

  Jim Grissom, M.V.: expressed concern that Council Member Schlicht does not have a
  photograph or a biography on the City’s web site and stated that members of the public
  should know who she is.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 9, 11, 12, 13, 14, 17, 18 and 19 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate
discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to approve
the Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

City Council Minutes  3  July 20, 2009
 2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the City Council Meeting of July 6, 2009, as presented.

3.  Number not used

4.  Check Register dated June 26, 2009, in the amount of $2,174,352.64

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated July 3, 2009, in the amount of $2,002,679.22

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for May 2009

  Received and filed.

7.  Community Development Agency Treasurer's Monthly Report for May 2009

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer's Monthly Report for May 2009

  Received and filed.

10.  Professional Services Agreement for Printing and Related Services for the City
  Outlook, Leisure Time, and Annual Report

  (1) Approved the Professional Services Agreement with Documedia Group for printing
  and related services for four issues of the biannual City Outlook, eight issues of the
  quarterly Leisure Time and two issues of the Annual Report for a total not to exceed
  amount of $260,694.68 through June 30, 2011; and (2) authorized the issuance of a
  purchase order to Documedia Group in the amount of $130,347.34 for FY 2009-10.

15.  Rate Adjustment for Solid Waste Delivered to Southeast Resource Recovery
  Facility

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  4  July 20, 2009
 16.  2008 Residential Resurfacing (CIP 838)

  (1) Approved Contract Change Order 1 in the amount of $375,178 to Purchase Order
  080442 to All American Asphalt, Inc.; (2) certified the completion of and accepted the
  improvements for the subject project; (3) authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice
  of Completion; (4) authorized the City Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the
  County of Orange and to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year
  and 35 days, respectively, after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion
  contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with the City; and (5) authorized payment
  of the final retention 35 days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

20.  Fiber Communication and Traffic Controller Upgrade Project-Various Locations
  (CIP 797)

  Approved the bid specifications and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for
  the subject project.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

21.  General Plan Amendment GPA2009-28, Development Code Amendment DCA2009-
  13, and Development Code Amendment DCA2009-14 - initiated petitions to update
  the Housing Element of the General Plan and amend the City’s Municipal Code.
  GPA2009-28 updates the City’s adopted Housing Element of the General Plan as
  required by State law. The Housing Element consists of housing goals and policies
  for the City. Specific housing programs that will implement these goals and policies
  are identified. In addition, the Housing Element summarizes the City’s existing and
  projected housing providing the basis for targeting policies and programs to
  address these needs. The goals and policies of the draft Housing Element carry
  forward much from the City’s existing Housing Element, with refinements and new
  programs to address changed circumstances and new state laws. DCA2009-13 is a
  proposed Ordinance amending Section 9.10.020 of Article II of Title 9 of the
  Municipal Code regarding density bonuses and affordable housing. DCA2009-14 is
  a proposed Ordinance amending Chapter 9.12 of Article II of Title 9 of the
  Municipal Code regarding the Business Park / Industrial Zone to allow for the By
  Right construction of emergency shelters.

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  John Douglas, Conexus: presented an overview of the various components of the City’s
  Housing Element, discussed the RHNA process, provided a land inventory, and outlined
  the new requirement to identify emergency shelters and transitional housing sites.

City Council Minutes  5  July 20, 2009
   Mayor Ury opened the public hearing at 6:55 p.m.

  Dale Tyler, M.V.: stated that he has never seen a public notice describing how these
  RHNA numbers are negotiated. Mr. Tyler asked when the change to the Housing
  Element needs to be enacted and suggested waiting a while.

  The following presented a written comment stating that he agrees with Mr. Tyler’s verbal
  remarks: Mike Ryan, M.V.

  Mayor Ury closed the public hearing at 6:57 p.m.

  John Douglas, Conexus: described the process for determining RHNA numbers.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  (1) adopt Negative Declaration declaring proposed Resolution and Ordinances will not
  have a significant adverse on the environment for purposes of CEQA review; (2) adopt
  Resolution 09-31 Approving General Plan Amendment GPA2009-28 to Modify the
  City’s General Plan Housing Element; (3) introduce Ordinance 09-275 Amending
  Section 9.10.020 of Article II of Title 9 of the Municipal Code Regarding Density
  Bonuses and Affordable Housing; and (4) introduce Ordinance 09-276 Amending
  Chapter 9.12 of Article II of Title 9 of the Municipal Code Regarding the Business Park /
  Industrial Zone to Allow for the Establishment of Emergency Shelters.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

RECESS

  At the hour of 7:24 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
  7:33 p.m., with all five City Council Members present.

NEW BUSINESS

22.  City Council Communication with Auditors

  Jennifer Farr, Mayer Hoffman McCann P.C., asked the City Council Members to

City Council Minutes  6  July 20, 2009
   communicate any known or suspected instances of fraud, improper accounting practices,
  or anything that the auditors should know before they start the process. Ms. Farr also
  outlined the scope and timing of the upcoming audit.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

28.  Adoption of the 2009-11 City Budget

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented
  the staff report and outlined follow-up information presented in response to questions
  posed at the July 6, 2009, Council Meeting.

  Barbara Anderson, M.V.: recommended postponing adoption of the budget and asked
  where the City will absorb the $6 million that the State might take. Ms. Anderson asked
  if there is revenue to cover this or if it will come from reserves.

  Dale Tyler, M.V.: stated that the City Council should follow the policy of not spending
  more than its income. He suggested that the Council should not spend to upgrade
  existing facilities and he noted that he didn’t see any proposed reductions in City staff.

  Ann Hagerty, M.V.: expressed concern for children of the City and stated that the library
  is vital to our residents’ education. Ms. Hagerty asked the City Council to not cut the
  Library’s materials budget.

  The following presented written comments in support of the Marguerite Tennis Center
  renovation: Linda Powell, M.V.; Jim Sahl, M.V.; Gloria Byrne, M.V.; Edward Sanchez,
  M.V.; Steve Berk, M.V.; Shripathi Kamath, M.V.; and Tom Teichmann, M.V.

  The following presented a written comment in opposition to adoption of the budget as
  proposed: Carl Schulthess, M.V.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 09-33 Adopting a Budget for the City of Mission Viejo for 2009-11 and
  Appropriating Funds for FY 2009-10 Only; and (2) adopt Resolution 09-34 Establishing
  an Appropriations Limit for FY 2009-10.

  Council Member Schlicht offered an amendment to the motion to delay consideration of

City Council Minutes  7  July 20, 2009
   the budget for 90 days until the State Budget is known. The motion died for lack of a
  second.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, Tem MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  City Attorney Bill Curley noted that the Council’s action will change numbers throughout
  a variety of documents in the City. Staff will see that agreements and records conform
  with the adopted 2009-2011 Budget.

City Attorney’s Report

29.  O’Neill Elementary School Closure: Environmental Review Process - Public
  Records indicate that the Saddleback Valley Unified School District Board of
  Trustees approved a contract for preparation of a Negative Declaration. The City
  may wish to actively participate in the environmental review process. The
  environmental review process should be completed and considered by the Trustees
  prior to the final decision to close O’Neill Elementary School

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Bert Bennett, M.V.: thanked the City Council and Mr. Curley for the incredible efforts
  that surfaced documents which indicate inappropriate actions by the Capistrano Unified
  School District.

  Romney Miller, M.V.: thanked the City for requesting the public information from the
  District and for the expert review of those documents.

  Mike Westerland, M.V.: thanked staff and Mr. Curley for the hard work and stated that
  he supports the idea of creating a Mission Viejo School District.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to call on the
  Saddleback Valley Unified School District to stop from moving forward with this
  change, reverse their decision to close O’Neill Elementary School, re-use the building for
  offices; and require that the environmental studies be done.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  8  July 20, 2009
   AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

30.  O’Neill Elementary School Closure: Charter School Community Effort - The
  Saddleback Valley Unified School District Board of Trustees has declined the
  approval of a charter school at the O’Neill Elementary School site. The City may
  wish to consider assisting with the appeal of this decision pursuant to the California
  Education Code as contemplated by the City’s General Plan. The City Council may
  direct the City Attorney’s Office and staff to review the process and the City’s role
  and advise the City Council thereafter

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Romney Miller: stated that he will appreciate any assistance the City can provide in
  resubmitting a Charter School application to the District.

  Bert Bennett, M.V.: stated that the O’Neill site is uniquely and ideally suited as an
  Elementary School and their proposal for a charter school was intended not only to
  maintain the site as a school, but to partner with the School District on an exciting and
  diversified set of programs. Mr. Bennett stated that any support from the City to
  resubmit a proposal would be very welcome and he directed interested parties to the
  website: www.oneillcharterschool.com.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to direct the City
  Attorney to review the process and return with a report describing how the City can help
  the Charter School to go forward.

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

31.  Consideration of funding and conducting a City-wide poll, costs not to exceed
  $15,000, investigating the goals of the City’s electorate regarding both SVUSD and
  CUSD. Topics to include school closings, traffic safety, school district consolidation,
  and support for charter schools. Poll to be completed by September 1, 2009

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Bert Bennett, M.V.: stated that people by nature do not champion change but leaders of
  vision put forth ideas like these and it is clearly time for some bold action in this City.

City Council Minutes  9  July 20, 2009
   He stated that he supports the poll and believes that the survey will uncover a swell of
  support.

  Jeanne Cassidy, M.V.: stated that the Council is obviously interested in knowing the will
  of the people and by conducting a city-wide poll, we will have a better idea of the
  residents’ opinion on the subject of our schools. She announced that she strongly
  supports school district consolidation and stated that it is time for Mission Viejo to take
  control of its schools.

  Romney Miller, M.V.: stated that the School District has too many needs to consider and
  it seems that a lot of Mission Viejo taxes are going to schools in other cities. He would
  love to see what residents think about this and he supports the survey.

  Jack Perisho, M.V.: expressed support for a survey and stated that it will be money well
  spent in order to find out what the residents want to do in terms of its schools.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  direct staff to conduct a City-wide poll in an amount not to exceed $15,000, to investigate
  the goals of the City’s electorate regarding both SVUSD and CUSD. Topics are to
  include school closings, traffic safety, school district consolidation, and support for
  charter schools. The poll is to be completed by September 1, 2009.

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  Council Member Schlicht stated for the record that she supports the School District
  consolidation but she is not in support of the survey at this time. She thinks the survey is
  being conducted too soon.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

9.  Community Development Agency Loan -- for Agency Operations

  Council Member Schlicht asked if there is a formal plan for payback of the loan.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein stated that
  the loan agreement requires that the loan will be repaid within a six-year period or
  sooner.

City Council Minutes  10  July 20, 2009
   Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to (1)
  adopt CDA Resolution 09-03 Requesting a Loan From the City of Mission Viejo in the
  Amount of $520,000; (2) adopt Resolution 09-27 Authorizing a Loan to the Community
  Development Agency; and (3) adopt CDA Resolution 09-04 Accepting a Loan From the
  City of Mission Viejo and Executing the Loan Agreement Between the City of Mission
  Viejo and the Community Development Agency.

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

11.  Maintenance of Traffic Signals and Appurtenance, Interconnect, Flashing Beacons,
  Illuminated Street Name Signs, Safety Lights and CCTV Cameras

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern that Republic ITS recently submitted the
  fourth highest bid on another project.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  (1) approve Second Amendment to Contract 07-48 with Republic ITS to extend the
  period of the contract from July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2011, and to increase the
  contract amount by $850,000; and (2) authorize staff to issue a purchase order to
  Republic ITS in an amount not to exceed $425,000 for the period July 1, 2009, through
  June 30, 2010.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht to re-bid the project. The motion died for
  lack of a second.

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

12.  Changes to the Personnel Policy on Cell Phone/PDA Allowances for Employees.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that the City has been sued by AT&T so she doesn’t
  know why we would extend this offer to the employees.

  Council Member Ledesma expressed his preference for staying with Verizon for all cell
  phone and PDA service.

City Council Minutes  11  July 20, 2009
   Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Bornstein presented the staff
  report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to adopt Resolution
  09-28 Amending the City’s Personnel Policy on Cell Phone/PDA Allowances for
  Employees.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Ledesma and Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

13.  City of Mission Viejo Seven-Year Public Works Capital Improvement Program
  (Fiscal Year 2009-2010 through Fiscal Year 2015-2016)

  Council Member Schlicht stated that the City should start looking at a master plan to start
  setting money aside for asphalt overlays. She is concerned that we stay on top of the
  street conditions and look towards the future.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 09-29 Adopting a Seven-Year Public Works Capital Improvement
  Program Beginning with the 2009?2010 Fiscal Year; and (2) direct the Director of Public
  Works to transmit the Seven-Year Public Works Capital Improvement Program to the
  Orange County Transportation Authority by August 8, 2009.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

14.  2009 Residential Resurfacing-Community Development Block Grant (CIP 838)

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  approve the bid specifications and authorize staff to advertise for construction bids for the
  subject project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  12  July 20, 2009
   AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

17.  Microsoft Licensing Renewal Agreement

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with the request for 275 software licenses as
  noted on page 3 of the staff report. She inquired if this includes a software license for
  home computers and if there is a price guarantee.

  Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander stated that there are 275 computers
  within the network at city hall, the library, and the other City facilities. Ms. Alexander
  stated that this does not include licenses for home computers and that the price is
  guaranteed for three years.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve the
  accompanying three-year agreement with Microsoft for Microsoft Product Licensing
  renewal and issue a purchase order to CompuCom for such services for 2009-10 in the
  amount of $62,382.68.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

18.  Street Sweeping Services

  Council Member Schlicht stated that this contract has been in effect since 1999 and she
  thinks it is good business practice to bid all City contracts. She expressed further concern
  that there is no reduction in frequency of street cleaning and striping.

  City Manager Wilberg announced that the original budget proposal included reduction of
  street sweeping services from once a week to every other week however, at the Budget
  Workshop Council directed staff to reinstate funding so that the existing level of service
  would be maintained. Street striping is not included in the budget as that service is
  provided by the County of Orange. Mr. Wilberg indicated that staff recommends
  extending the contract because Mission Viejo residents pay the lowest price per
  residential curb mile within South Orange County. By extending the contract, the City
  will maintain that low price.

City Council Minutes  13  July 20, 2009
   Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1)
  terminate the existing second amendment for the four-month contract extension with
  Sunset Property Services; (2) approve Third Amendment to the contract with Sunset
  Property Services for the period of July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2011, in an amount not
  to exceed $748,782.00; and (3) authorize staff to issue a purchase order to Sunset
  Property Services in an amount not to exceed $374,391.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

19.  OCCOG Amended and Restated Joint Powers Agreement

  Council Member Schlicht asked if the Orange County Council of Governments
  (OCCOG) has ever challenged any of the RHNA allocations.

  City Manager Wilberg replied that it is up to individual cities to challenge the RHNA
  allocations for their particular city. As indicated earlier this evening, OCCOG approves
  the demographic projections for Orange County based on the data provided by the Center
  for Demographic Research (CDR) so it is important for the city to belong to OCCOG and
  to have a voice in the process.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Ury, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 09-30 Approving and Executing an Amended and Restated Orange County
  Council of Governments (OCCOG) Joint Powers Agreement; and, (2) authorize the
  Mayor to execute the amended and restated Joint Powers Agreement, and transmit the
  signed OCCOG Joint Powers Agreement to the OCCOG Interim Executive Director.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

23.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

City Council Minutes  14  July 20, 2009
   Council Member Kelley presented the report.

24.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean apologized for showing up late and for missing the recent
  meeting of the Foothill/Eastern TCA.

25.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ledesma presented the report.

26.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG)

  Council Member Kelley announced that the meetings are held on the first Thursday of
  each month. There will be no meeting in August so she will have a report at the second
  Council Meeting in September.

STAFF REPORTS (Continued)

City Manager’s Report

27.  Decrease in Employer Contributions to CalPERS Retirement Program

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to adopt
  Resolution No. 09-32 Modifying the Employer Paid Member Contributions to the
  California Public Employees’ Retirement System.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

32.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

City Council Minutes  15  July 20, 2009
   By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City
  Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley stated that resident Dan Levine has been an asset to our City and she is
sad to report that he is moving out of town to be closer to his son. She reminded her colleagues
that Dan has been a tireless volunteer and he has been an advocate for senior services. Mr.
Levine received a Community of Character award last year and she stated that we are very sorry
to see Dan move. She also announced that a local realtor approached her about the possibility of
holding a foreclosure workshop in Mission Viejo. As a service to the residents, the workshop
would provide valuable information for those who are facing difficult decisions with a pending
foreclosure. City staff has indicated that the workshop could be held in the fall. Council
Member Kelley stated that she has received several requests from residents to consider renaming
the Youth Athletic Park after Marty Russo. Mr. Russo, who passed away a few months ago, was
instrumental in the formation of the City and he worked for the Mission Viejo Company. He
was also a long-time volunteer with the Mission Viejo Activities Committee. Council Member
Kelley stated that she did not know Marty Russo but she has been impressed with the list of his
contributions to our City and the many requests to honor him. She will pass the concept along to
the Community Services Commission and ask them to evaluate the request to name the park after
Mr. Russo. Finally, Council Member Kelley announced that a hometown Marine, Lance
Corporal Alex Minsky, was very seriously injured in Afghanistan. The 20 year-old resident,
who graduated from Capistrano Valley High School in 2007, is being treated at the Palo Alto
Polytraumatic Center where he is undergoing therapy for his injuries and working to recover.
Mrs. Kelley is attempting to rally Mission Viejo residents and is working with groups and
individuals who share the same interest to provide support for Alex. The City’s Marine
Adoption Committee has already started to obtain help for the family and she is planning a blood
drive for Alex on Tuesday, August 18, 2009, from 12:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. Council Member
Kelley encouraged those who are interested in helping Alex and his family to drop gift cards off
at City Hall (Target or Albertson’s grocery) or to contact her at (949) 444-1123 for more
information.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Ledesma wished residents an enjoyable summer and stated that he will see

Council Member Schlicht
